settlements.name: Aurenne
settlements.notes: walls:imperialStone. Royal seat of Aurelle on the navigable Aurine. The royal household lives inside the walled shell of an old imperial arena, the Arena-Keep, and barges from Sablonne unload at its quays. The court is split between the queen-mother's kin and the young horsemen sworn to the crown.

settlements.name: Pontavelle
settlements.notes: relicHolder:goldenSheaf. Rich market town where the imperial road crosses the Aurine on a seven-arched stone bridge and the grain barges load. Its church keeps the Gilded Sheaf above the altar; the granary-keepers who tend it are famed for their seed-lore, and northern traders call it Fjorna's sheaf.

settlements.name: Merlonne
settlements.notes: Lanternhouse of St. Isarn on a bend of the Aurine below Aurenne. The royal house endows it and buries its dead there. Its water-gate makes it easy to reach by boat, which the brothers try not to think about.

settlements.name: Ardelly
settlements.notes: Meadow village north of Aurenne where the royal stud grazes; young Aurelle horsemen learn to throw the javelin from the saddle here.

settlements.name: Brecy
settlements.notes: Chief port of the moor country, facing the Southern Narrows; ferry-boats cross to Albrenn when tide and toll allow. Salt pans and moor sheep make its wealth. Its count pays the Aurelle crown late and grudgingly.

settlements.name: Finvelle
settlements.notes: Fishing village on the western tip of Brecaine, above the reef sailors call the Dog's Teeth. The villagers salvage what the reef wrecks, and do not always wait for the crews to drown first.

settlements.name: Tavernac
settlements.notes: Oyster beds and a drovers' landing on Brecaine's south shore; moor cattle are shipped from here to the Aurine towns.

settlements.name: Morinac
settlements.notes: Harbour city of Valmorin on the Albrenn Sea; wool-ships from Albrenn tie up at its long timber quay. The town watch keeps a beacon ready on the headland all raiding season.

settlements.name: Escaulac
settlements.notes: Lanternhouse of St. Bertolf on the windswept headland west of Morinac; its scriptorium copies law-books for all three realms. Its bell is rung when strange sails are sighted, and every coast farmer knows what that means.

settlements.name: Vasselle
settlements.notes: Salt-marsh village at the head of a shallow bay: eel traps, salt-boiling sheds and a smugglers' path to Morinac.

settlements.name: Dauvy
settlements.notes: Orchard village of apples and cider presses; it owes cart-service to Morinac and resents every load.

settlements.name: Lorvaux
settlements.notes: Hill town where the imperial road south of Aurenne gives out into goat tracks. Its lords breed the hardy hill ponies the Aurelle horsemen ride on campaign.

settlements.name: Garmelle
settlements.notes: Charcoal-burners and bog-iron smelters on the upper Aurine; its smoke can be seen from Lorvaux on a still day.

settlements.name: Pellerac
settlements.notes: Shepherds' hamlet in the southern hills; outlaws winter in the empty summer huts above it.

settlements.name: Sablonne
settlements.notes: Port at the mouth of the Aurine, where sea-going ships hand their cargo to river barges bound for Aurenne. The sandbar shifts every winter and its pilots charge accordingly. Sea-raiders have burned its quays twice in living memory.

settlements.name: Vellac
settlements.notes: Ferry village on the lower Aurine; the ferryman's family has held the crossing for a hundred years and knows every boat on the river.

settlements.name: Quarelle
settlements.notes: Quarry village on Ondrelle's north shore; its pale stone built half of Sablonne, and its quarrymen fight like it.

settlements.name: Castel Varo
settlements.notes: walls:imperialStone. Royal seat of Varenne, where three imperial roads meet at the old stone bridge over the Orvanne, the Kings' Bridge. The richest market in Corvaine: Saraleonese silk-factors and northern fur-traders lodge in the same street. Its court is famous for feuds among royal kin.

settlements.name: Orvanac
settlements.notes: Varenne's sea-gate at the mouth of the Orvanne; the royal toll-house weighs every cargo bound upriver. Its harbour chain is a rusted ruin, and every tavern has a theory about who spent the money meant to mend it.

settlements.name: Lambrac
settlements.notes: Herring-salting town on Varenne's northern shore; its boats follow the shoals into the Albrenn Sea each autumn.

settlements.name: Fenaux
settlements.notes: Waystation town on the imperial road to the Rhenna: inns, smithies and a horse fair where Varenne's horsemen buy remounts.

settlements.name: Ravelonne
settlements.notes: Woodcutters' village in the Varenne forest; the royal hunting lodge nearby brings both silver and trouble.

settlements.name: Kolden
settlements.notes: walls:imperialStone. Old imperial city at the mouth of the Rhenna, its walls patched with timber where the stone has fallen. Wine and millstones go downriver; Frisholm cloth and northern amber come up. Its prior and its count both claim the river toll.

settlements.name: Hautgarde
settlements.notes: relicHolder:weepingShield. Stone fortress at the Rhenna bridgehead, where the imperial road meets the track to Saxmark. Its chapel keeps the Weeping Shield; the garrison believe it wept the night before the last Saxmark attack, and that is why they held. The chapel walls sweat with damp at every thaw.

settlements.name: Selvonne
settlements.notes: River town on the middle Rhenna with a fortified mill-weir; its millers and boatmen are forever quarrelling over the water.

settlements.name: Tourvaux
settlements.notes: Cove village under the old signal tower: goatherds, lobster pots, and a good view of every ship in the bay.

settlements.name: Tilvelle
settlements.notes: Swineherds and charcoal-burners in the great forest east of the Rhenna; deserters and outlaws hide in the deep wood.

settlements.name: Strelle
settlements.notes: walls:imperialStone. Walled city of Alsenne at the end of the imperial road, under vine-covered hills. Its stonemasons are the best in Corvaine and are hired by kings and abbots alike.

settlements.name: Albonne
settlements.notes: Lanternhouse of St. Ludra on the shore of Lac Albe beneath the mountains; pilgrims climb from here to the cave where the saint lived as a hermit. The abbess is a king's aunt and keeps her own counsel.

settlements.name: Thibaux
settlements.notes: River town at the head of navigation on the Rhenna; above it the river runs too shallow and fast for boats. Alsenne hill wine is barrelled here for the voyage north.

settlements.name: Dorelle
settlements.notes: Clearing village in the Alsenne woods; it pays its dues to the abbey of Albonne in honey and wax.

settlements.name: Neivaux
settlements.notes: Last hamlet below the mountain passes; its men guide travellers over the snows for silver, and sometimes rob them for more.

settlements.name: Vaux-Doré
settlements.notes: City of Burgonne's golden vale, famed for its wine and its tithe barns; the crown of Varenne keeps a counting-house here. Its merchants lend silver to kings and expect it back.

settlements.name: Ysellac
settlements.notes: Lanternhouse of St. Seraphine in the southern hills, the richest in Varenne; its vineyards and reliquary are a byword for wealth. The brothers keep a hired guard and say it is for the pilgrims.

settlements.name: Galmy
settlements.notes: Market town on the imperial road between Castel Varo and Vaux-Doré; its harvest fair draws merchants from the whole realm.

settlements.name: Adelonne
settlements.notes: Vineyard village in the eastern vale; its vintners owe a third of every harvest to the abbey of Ysellac.

settlements.name: Ludry
settlements.notes: Ploughland village whose reeve keeps the oldest tax roll in Burgonne and reads it aloud every Reaping.

settlements.name: Wendelburg
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Saxmark on the shore facing the Straits. Its Tide Gate, a timbered water-gate on old stone piers, lets the royal ships row into a walled inner harbour. The youngest of the three royal cities, and proud of it; its kings tax the Straits trade and answer Eyjar raids in kind.

settlements.name: Ludstede
settlements.notes: Market town where the tracks to Frisholm, Thuringel and the east march meet; cattle drovers and salt-carters crowd its fairs.

settlements.name: Haverlo
settlements.notes: Fishing village on the Saxmark shore; its boats sell herring to Wendelburg and news to anyone who pays.

settlements.name: Wolkenrath
settlements.notes: Farming village in the south of Saxmark; its folk still leave bread at the old mound on the heath and call it custom, not worship.

settlements.name: Wijkstede
settlements.notes: Beach-market town of Frisholm, where ships are drawn up on the strand to trade; Eyjar, Albric and Corvani merchants deal here under the count's peace. Its cloth halls make it richer than its size suggests.

settlements.name: Ambrelle
settlements.notes: Lanternhouse of St. Dunstel on Frisholm's open western shore, north of the Halswehr ditch and within sight of the Eyjar border. It has been raided before and keeps its reliquary in a stone undercroft; the abbot and the Halswehr commander each blame the other for the last time.

settlements.name: Halswehr
settlements.notes: Earth-and-timber fortress across the neck of land between Frisholm and the Eyjar country, its ditch running from shore to shore. The garrison watches Eyjar traders and raiders alike; bribes buy passage as often as swords.

settlements.name: Erfholt
settlements.notes: Forest city of Thuringel on the track through the deep woods; timber, tar and furs leave by ox-cart. Its lords keep more hounds than books.

settlements.name: Paludelle
settlements.notes: Lanternhouse of St. Tobiel on an island of firm ground in the Thuringel marsh, reached by a single causeway the brothers can flood. Fevers come with the summer mists.

settlements.name: Weldenau
settlements.notes: River port at the head of navigation on the Weldra, where forest timber is rafted down to the sea; raftsmen and hauliers fill its alehouses.

settlements.name: Fichtenrod
settlements.notes: Clearing village of pitch-boilers and bee-keepers in the southern forest.

settlements.name: Regenhof
settlements.notes: walls:imperialStone. Old legion-fort city of Bavarre, its square walls still standing, guarding the road toward the Golden City's frontier. Saraleonese envoys pass through on the way to the three courts, and the city is full of their coin and their spies.

settlements.name: Dunmund
settlements.notes: Small port at the mouth of the Dun on the Ember Sea; only river-craft from the east find their way here, carrying Saraleonese wine, silk and rumour.

settlements.name: Haldering
settlements.notes: Track town between Erfholt and Regenhof; salt-carts from the mountains pay toll at its gate.

settlements.name: Elsenmoor
settlements.notes: Alder-swamp village of turf-cutters and eel-fishers on Bavarre's northern edge.

settlements.name: Ebbensburg
settlements.notes: Port of the east march at the mouth of the Ostra; furs and wax come down from the Velkar country to its wharves. Its march-lord keeps the border and pays the Saxmark crown in furs rather than silver.

settlements.name: Brakvoort
settlements.notes: Ford-and-ferry town at the mouth of the Weldra, where the coast track crosses; timber rafts from Weldenau are broken up and sold here.

settlements.name: Falkenwacht
settlements.notes: relicHolder:anvilShard. March fortress on the eastern frontier, facing the Velkar rivers and the steppe beyond. Its chapel keeps an iron shard taken from northern raiders generations ago; the smith-lineage sworn to its keeper descends from captive northern smiths and forges the best blades in the march.

settlements.name: Brennrode
settlements.notes: New clearing village on the track east; its settlers were promised ten years free of dues, and the ten years are nearly up.

sites.name: the Shepherd's Gullet
sites.notes: Cave in the Brecaine moor where a stream vanishes underground. Shepherds shelter in its mouth and tell of an outlaw band that went in with its plunder and never came out.

sites.name: Ludra's Cell
sites.notes: Mountain cave above Lac Albe where St. Ludra is said to have lived as a hermit. Pilgrims leave tokens at the mouth; few go past the first bend, where the floor drops into dark water.

sites.name: the Old Kings' Mound
sites.notes: Great earthen barrow on the Saxmark heath from before the Lantern came east. A Wolkenrath family has kept it for generations as hereditary wardens and turns away the curious.

sites.name: the Widow's Hof
sites.notes: A march-lord's hall burned by steppe riders a generation ago. His widow held the ruin through one hard winter and it still bears her name; squatters and outlaws now shelter in its standing walls.

sites.name: the Dogteeth Wreck
sites.notes: A Saraleonese merchant galley broken on the Dog's Teeth reef off Brecaine. Its hull shows only at the lowest spring tides, and the Finvelle wreckers guard what is left.

sites.name: the Gray Watchtower
sites.notes: Roofless imperial signal tower on the hills above the Albrenn Sea; a hermit keeper lives in its base and lights a fire on stormy nights.
